Authorization is thorough: agency_imports read+write endpoints all call check_agency_membership; inquiries authenticated read/respond scope by principal.user_id at the repo layer with ownership verification (get_inquiry_for_realtor, mark_inquiry_read_for_realtor, respond_to_inquiry all take user_id) and the code comments cite the exact prior IDOR/pagination fixes; agent_reviews validates rating 1..=5 and body length; article comments validate non-empty + length cap. Background workers are careful: favorite_alerts.rs `continue`s on set_request_context failure (RLS-context safety) and runs enqueue+watermark advance in one REPEATABLE READ tx; search_alert_drainer.rs never crashes the loop (per-alert errors are logged, delivery marked only if any channel succeeds). The single finding below is a low-severity, self-contained, landable i18n gap in the alert-drainer notification composition -- a directory none of today's prior reality-server runs inspected -- and is distinct from all six previously-emitted reality-server findings.

evidence: services/search_alert_drainer.rs:260-273 -- SearchAlertDrainerWorker::run_once builds each saved-search alert's AlertNotification with HARDCODED ENGLISH copy: subject = format!("{count} new listing{} match your saved search \"{}\"", ...) (sso... i.e. lines 260-264) and body = format!("Your saved search \"{}\" has {count} new matching listing{}. Open the app to view {}.", ...) (lines 265-271). The subject/body strings never consult any locale.

The same struct DOES capture the recipient's locale: services/search_alert_drainer.rs:272-276 sets `locale: alert.recipient_locale.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "en".into())`, and the AlertNotification field is documented at services/search_alert_drainer.rs:45 as `/// Recipient locale (`sk` | `cs` | `de` | `en`), for localized copy later.` So the drainer already threads the locale through to the transport boundary but discards it when composing the message -- every sk/cs/de recipient gets English subject+body.

This is an inconsistency with the localization capability that ALREADY EXISTS in this exact directory: services/email.rs:102-109 (reset_subject) and services/email.rs:111-125 (reset_body) fully localize the password-reset email across Locale::Slovak / Czech / German / English via `use db::models::user::Locale` (email.rs:27). The reality portal is a 4-locale product (sk/cs/de/en per CLAUDE.md and the field doc), and the localized-copy pattern + Locale enum are in place -- the drainer simply does not use them.

Impact (why low / +1, not higher): reality-server currently wires only the LogEmailTransport / LogPushTransport stubs (search_alert_drainer.rs:74-118) -- no real SMTP/FCM/APNs adapter is injected yet -- so no mislocalized message reaches a user TODAY. This is a latent correctness gap that will ship English notifications to all locales the moment a real transport is wired via SearchAlertDrainerWorker::with_transports, unless the copy is localized first. It is user-facing-notification copy, not a crash/security issue, so it is scored Low (+1).

Fix (self-contained, services/ only, no build-gated / KMP dependency): parse alert.recipient_locale into db::models::user::Locale (fall back to English) and compose subject/body via a locale match mirroring email.rs's reset_subject/reset_body, or route the copy through the existing i18n mechanism, so the AlertNotification's subject/body honor the locale the drainer already carries. IG3: unit test that run_once (with a capturing test transport) produces a non-English subject/body for a Slovak recipient_locale and English for `en`/None.

Confidence medium: the English-only composition and the unused locale field are unambiguous from static read of search_alert_drainer.rs:42-46 and :255-276; the parallel localized pattern is confirmed at email.rs:27,102-125. Not upgraded to high only because it is a latent (stub-transport) gap rather than a live user-observable defect at present.
